chunks: O you who believe, be fearful of God. Let each soul consider what it has sent (of good deeds) in advance for the morrow, and fear God. Surely God is aware of what you do.

key_terms.اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ: Be fearful of God / Have God-consciousness
key_terms.لِغَدٍ: For the morrow / For the future

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran command believers to do regarding their deeds for the future?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Hashr is often linked to the concept of 'Muhasabah' (self-accounting), urging believers to critically evaluate their deeds before the ultimate reckoning. It underscores the divine attribute of 'Al-Khabir' (The All-Aware), reinforcing that God’s knowledge encompasses both outward actions and inward intentions, a key theme in understanding the spiritual state of the faithful.
